name: Firecrawl Crawl
description: Firecrawl site crawler — traverse a website from a seed URL and return clean, LLM-ready content for every page. Pay-per-call x402 (StableEnrich + QuestFlow gateways).

url.description: URL to scrape and extract content from

usage.outputShape: body.url (final URL), body.title (page title), body.content (page content as markdown)
usage.guide: POST to https://stableenrich.dev/api/firecrawl/scrape with a JSON body {"url": "<page to scrape>"}. Payment is x402 USDC on Base (~$0.013/call). The response is a plain synchronous JSON object — read the scraped page content as markdown from body.content, the page title from body.title, and the final (post-redirect) URL from body.url. Despite the "Crawl" name, this endpoint scrapes a single page, not a multi-page crawl.

name: Olostep Crawl
description: Olostep web crawler — crawl and parse multiple pages of a site at scale. Pay-per-call x402 via Orthogonal.

start_url.description: The starting point of the crawl.

max_pages.description: Maximum number of pages to crawl. Recommended for most use cases like crawling an entire website.

include_urls.description: URL path patterns to include in the crawl using glob syntax. Defaults to `/**` which includes all URLs. Use patterns like `/blog/**` to crawl specific sections (e.g., only blog pages), `/products/*.html` for product pages, or multiple patterns for different sections. Supports standard glob features like * (any characters) and ** (recursive matching).

exclude_urls.description: URL path names in glob pattern to exclude. For example: `/careers/**`. Excluded URLs will supersede included URLs.

max_depth.description: Maximum depth of the crawl. Useful to extract only up to n-degree of links.

include_subdomain.description: Include subdomains of the website. `false` by default.

search_query.description: An optional search query to find specific links and also sort the results by relevance.

top_n.description: An optional number to only crawl the top N most relevant links on every page as per search query.

webhook_url.description: An optional POST request endpoint called when this crawl is completed. The body of the request will be same as the response of this [`v1/crawls/{crawl_id}`](./info#response-created) endpoint.

timeout.description: End the crawl after n seconds with the pages completed until then. May take ~10s extra from provided timeout.

usage.callShape: POST https://x402.orth.sh/olostep/v1/crawls with JSON body {start_url, max_pages} (x402 USDC on Base, $0.01). Then poll GET https://x402.orth.sh/olostep/v1/crawls/{id} (FREE) until status=="completed".
usage.outputShape: POST returns body.id (crawl id) and body.status="in_progress". Poll GET on the id returns body.status ("in_progress"->"completed"), body.pages_count, body.credits_consumed.
quirks: Async/queued: the paid POST returns status='in_progress' with a crawl id (body.id like 'crawl_xxx'), NOT the crawl results.
Poll GET https://x402.orth.sh/olostep/v1/crawls/{id} to get progress; this status GET is FREE (no x402 payment) and returns 200.
Crawl completes fast for small max_pages (1 page completed within seconds in testing).
Required body fields: start_url and max_pages. Optional: include_urls/exclude_urls (glob), max_depth, search_query, webhook_url, timeout.
Price is fixed at $0.01 per crawl-create call (accepts.amount=10000 USDC base units) despite priceDisplay='Varies'; per-page credits tracked in credits_consumed.
Supply a webhook_url in the POST body to get pushed the final result instead of polling.
usage.guide: Start a crawl with POST https://x402.orth.sh/olostep/v1/crawls and JSON body {"start_url":"<url>","max_pages":<n>} — this is the only paid step (x402 USDC on Base, ~$0.01). The response is a queued job: read body.id and note status='in_progress'. Then poll GET https://x402.orth.sh/olostep/v1/crawls/{id} (free, no payment) every few seconds until body.status=='completed'; read body.pages_count and body.credits_consumed. Alternatively pass webhook_url in the POST body to be notified on completion instead of polling.

name: x402node Robots.txt Parser
description: Fetch and parse a domain's robots.txt. Returns parsed allow/disallow rules per user-agent, declared sitemap URLs, crawl-delay directives, and raw content. Built for AI agents planning ethical web crawling and SEO audits.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/web/robots?domain=<bare-host> (x402 v1 paid, ~$0.005 USDC on Base). The `domain` query param is REQUIRED and must be a bare host (example.com), NOT a full URL.
usage.outputShape: domain (string), exists (bool), raw (string|null), rules (object keyed by user-agent), sitemaps (string[]), crawl_delay (object), _hint (promotional, ignore)
quirks: Required query param is `domain` (bare host like example.com), NOT a full URL and NOT `url`.
Calling with no ?domain= returns HTTP 500 {"error":"Missing domain parameter"} AND STILL CHARGES the $0.005 x402 fee — always include ?domain=.
When a site has no robots.txt the call still returns 200 with exists:false and empty rules/sitemaps/crawl_delay — that is a valid result, not an error.
Response includes a promotional `_hint` field unrelated to the result; ignore it.
Provider serves x402 v1 (Payment-Required has no `accepts` array) — agentcash MCP fetch CANNOT pay it; use a v1-capable payer.
usage.guide: Fetch and parse a domain's robots.txt. Returns parsed allow/disallow rules per user-agent, declared sitemap URLs, crawl-delay directives, and raw content. Built for AI agents planning ethical web crawling and SEO audits. GET https://api.x402node.dev/web/robots?domain=<bare-host> (x402 v1 paid, ~$0.005 USDC on Base). The `domain` query param is REQUIRED and must be a bare host (example.com), NOT a full URL. Output: domain (string), exists (bool), raw (string|null), rules (object keyed by user-agent), sitemaps (string[]), crawl_delay (object), _hint (promotional, ignore)

name: x402node Sitemap Parser
description: Fetch and parse a site's sitemap.xml (auto-detects sitemap index). Returns up to 500 URLs with lastmod/changefreq/priority plus any sub-sitemaps. Built for AI agents indexing sites, tracking content changes, and SEO audits.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.x402node.dev/web/sitemap?url=<full-URL-with-scheme> (x402 v1 paid, ~$0.008 USDC on Base). The `url` query param is REQUIRED and must be a FULL URL including scheme (https://www.example.com), NOT a bare domain.
usage.outputShape: url (normalized string), is_index (bool), total_urls (number), total_sub_sitemaps (number), urls (array), sub_sitemaps (array), _hint (promotional, ignore)
quirks: PARAM TRAP: required query param is `url` (FULL URL with scheme), NOT `domain` — this differs from the sibling /web/robots endpoint which uses `domain`.
Calling with `domain=` (or no url) returns HTTP 500 {"error":"Missing url parameter"} AND STILL CHARGES the $0.008 x402 fee. The original bundled registry doc wrongly used domain= here.
A site with no resolvable sitemap still returns 200 with total_urls:0 and empty urls/sub_sitemaps — valid result, not an error.
Returns up to 500 URLs; auto-detects and reports sitemap indexes via is_index/sub_sitemaps.
Response includes a promotional `_hint` field; ignore it.
Provider serves x402 v1 (Payment-Required has no `accepts` array) — agentcash MCP fetch CANNOT pay it; use a v1-capable payer.

name: Strale Robots.txt Parse
description: Fetches and parses a website's robots.txt, returning per-user-agent allow/disallow rules, declared sitemaps, the list of user agents addressed, and a blocks_all_crawlers flag. Useful for crawl-policy auditing and AI-bot access checks.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/robots-txt-parse?url=<TARGET_SITE_OR_ROBOTS_URL> (x402 USDC on Base). The url query param is required; you may pass the site root (it resolves /robots.txt) or the full robots.txt URL. No JSON body.
usage.outputShape: url, exists (bool), rules[].{user_agent,allow[],disallow[]}, user_agents[], sitemaps[], total_rules, total_allow_rules, total_disallow_rules, blocks_all_crawlers (bool), raw_length, _meta.{capability,latency_ms,provenance.source,provenance.fetched_at,payment.{method,settlement_id,price_usd}}
quirks: url is a query-string parameter, NOT a JSON body — GET request only.
If the target has no robots.txt the call still returns 200 (and you still pay): {exists:false, message:'No robots.txt found.'}. Pick a site known to have robots.txt to see full parsing.
user_agents[] may contain DUPLICATES (e.g. '*' and 'GPTBot' appear twice when the file has multiple blocks for the same agent) — dedupe client-side if needed.
Price observed $0.0216 USDC on Base; registry surface shows it as 'Varies'.
Every response carries a Strale audit/provenance record under _meta (cryptographic chain hashing per provider claims).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.strale.io/x402/sitemap-parse?url=<SITEMAP_XML_URL> (x402 USDC on Base). The url query param is required and should point at the sitemap.xml. No JSON body.
usage.outputShape: url, type ('urlset'|'sitemapindex'), total_urls (int), sample_urls[].{loc,lastmod,changefreq,priority}, top_path_segments[].{segment,count}, has_lastmod, has_changefreq, has_priority, newest_lastmod, oldest_lastmod, _meta.{capability,latency_ms,provenance.source,provenance.fetched_at,payment.{method,settlement_id,price_usd}}

name: TrustSource Robots Intelligence
description: TrustSource robots.txt intelligence — analyze a domain's crawl rules and AI-bot access policies. Pay-per-call x402.

exists.description: True if a robots.txt file was found

aiFriendly.description: True if AI training crawlers are not broadly blocked

truncated.description: True if response exceeded 100KB body cap

hasParseErrors.description: True if any directive failed to parse

ai.description: Per-AI-bot policy analysis across 24 known crawlers

globalBlock.description: True if User-agent: * Disallow: / is present

globalAllow.description: True if User-agent: * Allow: / is present

status.description: HTTP status of the robots.txt fetch

usage.callShape: GET https://api.trustsource.cc/robots?domain=example.com (required query param: domain). x402 USDC on Base (eip155:8453), $0.0020.
usage.outputShape: body.domain, body.exists, body.tier (OPEN|SELECTIVE|BLOCKED_AI|BLOCKED_ALL|NO_ROBOTS_TXT), body.aiFriendly, body.ai.policies[] (per-bot {userAgent, blocked, partial, disallow[], allow[]}), body.ai.knownBotsBlocked, body.sitemaps[], body.userAgents[], body.meta.checkedAt

usage.guide: Call GET https://api.trustsource.cc/robots?domain=<domain> with the domain you want to analyze as a query param (no request body). name: Website URL Extractor
description: Extract all URLs/links from a website for crawl seeding. Gated by an x402 micropayment via the PaySponge gateway.

usage.callShape: GET https://url-extractor.x402.paysponge.com/url/:domain where :domain is a bare hostname (e.g. vercel.com), no body
quirks: The :domain path segment is a bare hostname (e.g. 'vercel.com'), NOT a full URL with scheme/path.

It only reads the target site's /sitemap.xml. If the domain has no sitemap, you STILL get charged $0.01 and receive HTTP 422 {error:'No URLs found in sitemap', count:0} -- pick a domain you know publishes a sitemap.
example.com has no sitemap and returns 422; use a real content site to get a 200.
Response can be very large (vercel.com returned ~766KB / 6975 urls) -- expect big payloads for big sites.
usage.guide: Call GET https://url-extractor.x402.paysponge.com/url/<domain> with the bare hostname in the path (e.g. /url/vercel.com), no request body; pay the $0.01 x402 quote (USDC on Base). On success you get HTTP 200 with {sitemap, count, urls:[{url, lastmod}]} -- read the link list from body.urls. The service only parses the domain's /sitemap.xml, so if the site lacks one you are still charged and get a 422 with count:0; only point it at domains you know publish a sitemap. Large sites return very large responses (thousands of URLs).

name: Cloudflare Crawl (StableEnrich)
description: Cloudflare Browser Rendering website crawl (JS render optional). Async: POST returns a JWT token; poll the SIWX jobs endpoint (free) until complete. Pay-per-call x402.

usage.callShape: POST https://stableenrich.dev/api/cloudflare/crawl with JSON body {url, limit, depth, formats} (x402 pay) → 202 {token}; then poll GET https://stableenrich.dev/api/cloudflare/jobs?token=<jwt> (SIWX, free, same wallet)
usage.outputShape: Poll response: body.status ("completed"), body.total/body.finished/body.skipped, body.records[].markdown, body.records[].metadata.title, body.records[].url, body.records[].status
quirks: Async two-step: paid POST /api/cloudflare/crawl returns HTTP 202 with {token} (a JWT), NOT the result.
Poll GET /api/cloudflare/jobs?token=<jwt> using SIWX auth (same wallet, FREE) every 3-5s. Done when body.status==='completed' (or finished+skipped>=total).
limit max 25, depth max 3. render=true executes JS (slower).
Records that point off the seed origin (e.g. external links) come back status:'skipped' with no markdown.
JWT token is what you poll with; it carries the jobId+wallet binding.
usage.guide: Cloudflare Browser Rendering crawl via StableEnrich. POST https://stableenrich.dev/api/cloudflare/crawl with JSON {url, limit<=25, depth<=3, formats:["markdown"], render?} — this pays $0.10 (x402, Base) and returns 202 {token}. Then poll GET https://stableenrich.dev/api/cloudflare/jobs?token=<jwt> with SIWX (same wallet, free) until body.status==="completed". Read crawled content from body.records[].markdown (each record also has metadata.title and url; off-origin links return status:"skipped").

name: NetIntel Robots.txt Analyzer
description: Fetches and parses a domain's robots.txt — returns every crawl rule grouped by user-agent (allow/disallow/crawl-delay), discovered sitemap URLs, and an optional path-permission check (is a given path allowed or blocked for a given bot) — plus a 0–100 score and A–F grade, so agents can respect crawl policy and locate sitemaps before scraping.

domain.description: Domain name to fetch robots.txt from (e.g. example.com). Required query param.

path.description: Optional URL path to check permission for (e.g. /api/data); populates path_check in the response.

user_agent.description: Optional bot name to check rules for (default: *).

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/robots-txt/analyze?domain=<domain>[&path=<path>&user_agent=<bot>] (required query param `domain`; x402 payment ~$0.01 USDC on Base eip155:8453 OR Solana; no JSON body). Result returned inline in the 200; no polling.
usage.outputShape: body.domain; body.robots_url; body.found (bool); body.status_code; body.raw_content_preview (string|null, truncated robots.txt); body.sitemaps[] (sitemap URLs discovered); body.rules[]{user_agent, allow[], disallow[], crawl_delay}; body.path_check (null unless `path` supplied){path,user_agent,allowed,matched_rule,rule_type}; body.score (0–100); body.grade (A–F); body.findings[]{rule,label,impact,detail}.
quirks: Inputs are query-string params on a GET (no JSON body): ?domain=<domain>. `domain` is required; `path` and `user_agent` are optional and only `path` populates path_check.

A domain with no robots.txt still returns HTTP 200 with found:false, status_code 404, empty rules[]/sitemaps[], and a findings[] entry {rule:'not_found', impact:-30} (verified: example.com → found:false, score 70, grade C).
score/grade reflect the audited site's robots.txt (or absence of it), not this API.
Same NetIntel provider as the netintel-production-440c.up.railway.app host; this canonical netintel.dev host serves this operation. Base USDC exact scheme (Solana USDC also advertised), no API key.
Synchronous single call — pure read of a public robots.txt, safe to auto-verify.
usage.guide: Fetch and parse a domain's robots.txt before crawling/scraping it. Call GET https://netintel.dev/robots-txt/analyze with a required `domain` query param (e.g. ?domain=example.com); optionally add &path=/some/path and &user_agent=<bot> to check whether that path is allowed for that bot (result in body.path_check). It is an x402 endpoint costing ~$0.01 USDC on Base (or Solana); pay it and read the JSON synchronously — no polling. Read body.rules[] for the per-user-agent allow/disallow/crawl_delay directives, body.sitemaps[] for discovered sitemap URLs to enumerate site content, and body.grade/body.score for an overall crawl-policy verdict; body.findings[] explains score deductions. Missing robots.txt is not an error — you still get HTTP 200 with found:false. Verified 2026-07-30 with ?domain=example.com → HTTP 200, $0.01 charged, found:false (404), score 70, grade C.

name: NetIntel Sitemap Parser
description: Fetch and parse any XML sitemap or sitemap index (or auto-discover it from a bare domain via robots.txt/common paths) and return every URL with its priority, change frequency, and last-modified date plus coverage stats and an SEO grade.

url.description: Sitemap URL or domain name to parse (e.g. https://example.com/sitemap.xml or example.com)

limit.description: Maximum number of URLs to return (1-1000, default 100)

source_url.description: null when no sitemap was found/parseable (graceful 200 with grade F)

usage.callShape: GET https://netintel.dev/sitemap-parser/fetch?url=<SITEMAP_URL_OR_DOMAIN>[&limit=<1-1000>] (x402 paid, $0.01 USDC on Base or Solana; `url` is a REQUIRED query-string parameter — this is a GET, no JSON body)
usage.outputShape: body.source_url (string|null — null if no sitemap found), body.sitemap_type ('urlset' | 'sitemapindex' | null), body.total_urls (int), body.urls_returned (int), body.child_sitemaps_fetched (int), body.urls[] ({url, last_modified, change_frequency, priority}), body.stats ({newest_url_date, oldest_url_date, avg_priority, has_lastmod, has_priority, has_changefreq}), body.score (int), body.grade (letter A-F), body.findings[] ({rule, label, impact, detail}). Verified 200: total_urls=84, urls_returned=84, grade 'A', score 95.
quirks: The `url` is a query-string parameter, not a JSON body — this is a GET request. Pass a full sitemap URL (e.g. https://example.com/sitemap.xml) OR a bare domain (e.g. example.com), in which case it auto-discovers the sitemap via robots.txt/common paths.
Follows sitemap-index files only ONE level deep and fetches at most the first 3 child sitemaps (child_sitemaps_fetched reports how many).
Optional `limit` query param caps returned URLs (1-1000, default 100); total_urls reflects the full sitemap size while urls_returned reflects the capped slice.

A domain with no parseable sitemap still returns HTTP 200 (paid) with source_url:null and grade 'F' — this is a graceful result, not an error. NetIntel does not charge on 4xx/5xx (payment settled only when the call succeeds).
Fixed price ($0.01 = 10000 base units USDC); not a dynamic/varies quote. Payable on Base (eip155:8453) or Solana.
usage.guide: Call GET https://netintel.dev/sitemap-parser/fetch with a single required query param `url` set to either a full sitemap URL (https://example.com/sitemap.xml) or a bare domain (example.com); with a bare domain the service auto-discovers the sitemap from robots.txt or common paths. Optionally add &limit=N (1-1000, default 100) to cap how many URLs come back. Pay via x402 ($0.01 USDC on Base or Solana; no API key, no signup). The response is synchronous JSON: read body.sitemap_type to see whether it was a urlset or a sitemapindex, body.total_urls for the full count and body.urls_returned for how many were returned, then iterate body.urls[] for each {url, last_modified, change_frequency, priority}. body.stats summarizes date range and field coverage, and body.score/body.grade/body.findings[] give an SEO health assessment. If body.source_url is null the site had no parseable sitemap (grade F) — still a valid 200. Sitemap indexes are followed only one level deep (first 3 children).

name: Agentstools Sitemap
description: Discover and parse a site's sitemap in one paid call — pass a site root (it finds the sitemap via robots.txt or /sitemap.xml) or a direct .xml URL, and get back the list of URLs with lastmod/priority, handling <sitemapindex> one level deep.

url.description: Site root URL (sitemap is found via robots.txt or /sitemap.xml) or a direct sitemap .xml URL. Passed as a query param.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/sitemap?url=<site-root-or-sitemap.xml-URL> — no request body; pay $0.003 USDC via x402 on Base. Result returned synchronously in the 200 JSON body.
usage.outputShape: Sync JSON: urls[] (each {loc, lastmod, priority} — priority is a string like '1.0'/'0.5'), count (int, number of URLs returned), source (string, where the sitemap was found, e.g. 'robots.txt:https://www.cloudflare.com/sitemap.xml'), truncated (bool). Verified live for url=https://www.cloudflare.com: count 893, source 'robots.txt:https://www.cloudflare.com/sitemap.xml', truncated false.
quirks: Input is a GET query param 'url' (required), NOT a JSON body. The documented example {"url":"..."} maps to ?url=... . The x402 schema lists method enum [GET,HEAD,DELETE]; use GET.
'url' may be a site root (the service resolves the sitemap via robots.txt or /sitemap.xml) or a direct .xml URL.
Handles <sitemapindex> one level deep; the 'source' field reports how/where the sitemap was located.
A site with no resolvable sitemap still returns 200 (count 0 / empty urls) — valid result, not an error.
'truncated' flags when the URL list was capped; check it before assuming the full set was returned.
402 body is empty {}; the x402 challenge (accepts) is served base64-JSON in the 'payment-required' response header.
x402 paid $0.003 USDC on Base only (asset 0x833589..., payTo 0xF22e558a...); no Solana option, no API key / no sign-in.
usage.guide: Discover and parse a site's sitemap in one paid call. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/sitemap with query param 'url' set to a site root (e.g. url=https://www.cloudflare.com — the service finds the sitemap via robots.txt or /sitemap.xml) or a direct sitemap .xml URL. No request body. Pay $0.003 USDC via x402 on Base (no API key). Read the 200 JSON: 'urls' is the list of entries (each {loc, lastmod, priority}), 'count' is how many were returned, 'source' says where the sitemap was located, and 'truncated' tells you if the list was capped. Handles a sitemap index one level deep. For robots.txt allow/disallow rules instead of the URL list, use a robots parser; for single-page structured extraction use the sibling Agentstools /structured op.
